faqs.a: Normal places the overlay on top with your opacity setting. Multiply darkens where layers overlap, Screen brightens, Overlay adds contrast, Darken keeps the darker pixel, Lighten keeps the lighter one.

photo-overlay.formula:
scaled_w = overlay_w × (scale / 100)
scaled_h = overlay_h × (scale / 100)
center_x = (base_w − scaled_w) / 2,  center_y = (base_h − scaled_h) / 2
pixel_out = blend(base_pixel, overlay_pixel × opacity)
howTo: Upload the background photo as the base image and the second photo as the overlay.
Set the overlay opacity (0–100%) and choose a blend mode such as Normal, Multiply, or Screen.
Adjust the overlay scale percentage and pick one of the nine position presets.
Watch the live preview and fine-tune until the fusion looks right.
Choose PNG or JPG and press Download to save the result.
keyFacts: The output always keeps the base image's width and height.
The overlay is scaled by your percentage, then placed at one of nine preset positions.
Opacity blends the two layers: 0% hides the overlay, 100% makes it fully opaque.
Blend modes change how overlapping pixels mix — Multiply for shadows, Screen for light, Overlay for contrast.
The preview re-renders instantly on every change; nothing is uploaded.

limitations: The overlay keeps its aspect ratio — it cannot be stretched or rotated.
Fine edge blending (feathered masks) is not included; edges stay sharp.
Very large base images may render slowly on low-end phones.
EXIF metadata from the originals is not carried into the fused file.

photo-overlay.workedExample:
Base photo 1200 × 800 px with a 400 × 400 px logo overlay at 50% scale, centered, opacity 60%:
scaled size = 400 × 0.5 = 200 × 200 px
x = (1200 − 200) / 2 = 500,  y = (800 − 200) / 2 = 300
The logo is drawn at position (500, 300) with 60% opacity in Normal blend mode, and the result downloads as a 1200 × 800 px image.
